metadata.title: On Serre's modularity conjecture for 2-dimensional mod $p$ representations of $\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ unramified outside $p$

nodes.name: Lift of a residual representation
nodes.statement: A lift of $\overline{\rho}$ is a continuous representation $\rho: G_{\mathbb{Q}} \to \mathrm{GL}_2(V)$ with $V$ the integers of a finite extension of $\mathrm{Frac}(W(\mathbb{F}))$, such that the reduction of $\rho$ modulo the maximal ideal of $V$ is isomorphic to $\overline{\rho}$.

nodes.name: Minimal lift at $\ell \neq p$
nodes.statement: $\rho$ is minimal at a prime $\ell \neq p$ if it is minimally ramified at $\ell$ in the terminology of Diamond.

nodes.name: Modular representation
nodes.statement: A residual mod $p$ representation $\overline{\rho}$ (or a $p$-adic representation $\rho$) is modular if it is reducible (in the $p$-adic case assuming irreducibility) or arises from a newform with respect to the embedding $\iota_p$. A compatible system $(\rho_\lambda)$ is modular if it arises from a newform.

nodes.name: Linked compatible systems
nodes.statement: Two compatible systems are linked at a prime if their residual representations at that prime are isomorphic up to semisimplification.

nodes.name: Minimal of weight 2 at $p$
nodes.statement: $\rho$ is minimal of weight 2 at $p$ if its determinant is $\varepsilon \omega_p^{k(\bar\rho)-2}\chi_p|_{D_p}$ and, when $\bar\rho|_{I_p}$ has the form $\mathrm{diag}(\bar\chi_p^{k-1},1)$ with $2 \le k \le p-1$, $\rho|_{I_p}$ has the form $\mathrm{diag}(\omega_p^{k-2}\chi_p,1)$; further if $k(\bar\rho)=2$, $\rho|_{I_p}$ is Barsotti-Tate.

nodes.name: Semistable mod $p$ representation
nodes.statement: A mod $p$ representation $\bar\rho$ is semistable if at all primes ramified in $\bar\rho$ that are $\neq p$, the ramification is unipotent.

nodes.name: Dihedral representation
nodes.statement: $\bar\rho$ is dihedral if its projective image is a dihedral group.

nodes.name: Serre weight $k(\bar\rho)$ and conductor $N(\bar\rho)$
nodes.statement: $N(\bar\rho)$ is the prime-to-$p$ Artin conductor of $\bar\rho$, and $k(\bar\rho)$ is the Serre weight as defined in [Serre3].

nodes.name: Main theorem (level 1 case of Serre's conjecture)
nodes.statement: A $\bar\rho$ of level one arises from $S_{k(\bar\rho)}(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}))$ with respect to an embedding $\iota: \bar{\mathbb{Q}} \hookrightarrow \bar{\mathbb{Q}}_p$.
conclusions: $\bar\rho$ arises from a cuspidal eigenform in $S_{k(\bar\rho)}(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}))$

nodes.name: Modularity for prime conductor and weight 2
nodes.statement: If $\bar\rho$ is irreducible, odd, 2-dimensional mod $p$ representation of $G_\mathbb{Q}$ with $k(\bar\rho)=2$, $N(\bar\rho)=q$ ($q$ prime), and $p>2$, then it arises from $S_2(\Gamma_1(q))$.
conclusions: $\bar\rho$ arises from $S_2(\Gamma_1(q))$

nodes.name: Finiteness of mod-$p$ representations unramified outside $p$
nodes.statement: There are only finitely many isomorphism classes of continuous semisimple odd representations $\bar\rho: G_\mathbb{Q} \to \mathrm{GL}_2(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ that are unramified outside $p$.
assumptions: $\bar\rho: G_\mathbb{Q} \to \mathrm{GL}_2(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ continuous, semisimple, odd, unramified outside $p$
conclusions: Only finitely many isomorphism classes of such $\bar\rho$

nodes.name: Existence of minimal weight-2 lift
nodes.statement: $\bar\rho$ has a lift $\rho$ that is minimal of weight 2; its determinant is $\varepsilon \omega_p^{k(\bar\rho)-2} \chi_p$.
conclusions: Existence of a lift $\rho$ of $\bar\rho$ that is minimal of weight 2 with determinant $\varepsilon \omega_p^{k(\bar\rho)-2} \chi_p$

nodes.name: Galois-theoretic analog of Carayol's lemma (lift with prescribed nebentype)
nodes.section: 2.3 A Galois theoretic analog of Carayol's lemma
nodes.statement: There exists a $V$-valued lift $\rho$ of $\bar\rho$ of determinant $\varepsilon \chi_p^{k(\bar\rho)-1} \eta_q^i$, minimal at primes outside $p,q$, crystalline of weight $k(\bar\rho)$ at $p$, and with $\rho|_{I_q}$ of the form $\mathrm{diag}(\chi \eta_q^i, 1)$ on inertia at $q$ (nebentype $\chi \eta_q^i$ at $q$).
assumptions: $\bar\rho$ continuous, odd, irreducible with $2 \le k(\bar\rho) \le p+1$, $k(\bar\rho) \neq p$, non-solvable image
Odd prime $q$ ramified in $\bar\rho$ with $\bar\rho|_{I_q}$ of triangular form with character $\bar\chi$ from $\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}_q(\mu_q)/\mathbb{Q}_q)$
conclusions: Existence of a lift $\rho$ of $\bar\rho$ with the listed local properties (nebentype $\chi\eta_q^i$ at $q$, crystalline of weight $k(\bar\rho)$ at $p$)

nodes.name: Compatible system from a minimal lift
nodes.statement: (i) For $\bar\rho$ as in Proposition \ref{p}, given a minimal lift $\rho$, there is a weakly compatible system $(\rho_\lambda)$ (over a number field $E$) containing $\rho$ at the prime above $p$ fixed by $\iota_p$; for $\lambda$ above an unramified prime $\ell\neq p$, $\rho_\lambda$ is Barsotti-Tate at $\ell$ and shares the inertial WD parameter at $p$ with $\rho$. (ii) For $\bar\rho$ as in Proposition \ref{q} with $k(\bar\rho)=2$ and non-trivial nebentype $\chi\eta_q^i$ at $q$, $\rho$ extends to a compatible system $(\rho_\lambda)$ such that at $\lambda$ above $q$, $\rho_\lambda$ is unramified at $p$ and Barsotti-Tate over $\mathbb{Q}_q(\mu_q)$; moreover if $\overline{\rho_\lambda}$ has non-solvable image its weight is $j+2$ or that of its twist by $\bar\chi_q^{-j}$ is $q+1-j$ (where $\omega_q^j = \chi\eta_q^i$).
assumptions: (i) Setup of Proposition \ref{p} (ordinary, $2 \le k(\bar\rho)\le p+1$, $k(\bar\rho)\neq p$, $p>3$)
(ii) Setup of Proposition \ref{q} with $k(\bar\rho)=2$ and $\chi\eta_q^i$ non-trivial
conclusions: Existence of a weakly compatible system $(\rho_\lambda)$ with the stated local refinements at $p$, $\ell$, and $q$

nodes.name: Wintenberger's lemma on dihedral semistable representations
nodes.statement: (i) A mod $p$ dihedral semistable odd irreducible $\bar\rho$ exists iff $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and the class number of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-p})$ is non-trivial (so $p \neq 3,7,11,19,43,67,163$); such $\bar\rho$ is split at $p$ and has a twist of Serre weight $k=(p+1)/2$. (ii) If $\bar\rho$ is dihedral induced from the quadratic subfield of $\mathbb{Q}(\mu_p)$ and is locally irreducible at $p$ of weight $\le p+1$, then its weight is $(p+3)/2$.
assumptions: $\bar\rho$ dihedral induced from quadratic subfield of $\mathbb{Q}(\mu_p)$, locally irreducible at $p$, weight $\le p+1$ (for (ii))
conclusions: (i) Existence iff $p\equiv 3\pmod 4$ and $h(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-p})) > 1$; $\bar\rho$ is split at $p$, has twist of weight $(p+1)/2$
(ii) Weight equals $(p+3)/2$

nodes.name: Weight reduction by twist
nodes.statement: Assume $\tau: G_{\mathbb{Q}_p} \to \mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{F})$ has weight $k \neq 2$, $k < p$. If $\tau$ is irreducible and $k-1 = p-k'$ with $k' \ge 0$, then $\tau \otimes \bar\chi_p^{k'}$ has weight $k'+2 = p+3-k$. If $\tau|_{I_p}$ is split, $\tau \otimes \bar\chi_p^{1-k}$ has weight $p+1-k$.
conclusions: If $\tau$ irreducible with $k-1 = p-k'$: $w(\tau \otimes \bar\chi_p^{k'}) = p+3-k$
If $\tau|_{I_p}$ split: $w(\tau \otimes \bar\chi_p^{1-k}) = p+1-k$

nodes.name: Breuil-Mezard / Savitt: BT-over-$\mathbb{Q}_p(\mu_p)$ + reducible residual implies ordinary up to twist
nodes.statement: If $\rho: G_{\mathbb{Q}_p} \to \mathrm{GL}_2(O)$ becomes Barsotti-Tate over $\mathbb{Q}_p(\mu_p)$ and is residually reducible, then $\rho$ itself is reducible; more precisely, a twist of $\rho$ by a power of $\omega_p$ is ordinary.
conclusions: $\rho$ is reducible
A twist of $\rho$ by some power of $\omega_p$ is ordinary

nodes.name: Modularity for crystalline lifts when residual is modular
nodes.statement: Let $p$ be an odd prime. If $\rho: G_\mathbb{Q}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(O)$ is irreducible, unramified outside $p$, crystalline of Hodge-Tate weights $(k-1,0)$ with $k$ even and $2 \le k \le p+1$, and the residual $\bar\rho$ is modular, then $\rho$ arises from $S_k(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}))$.
assumptions: At $p$ crystalline, Hodge-Tate weights $(k-1,0)$, $k$ even, $2\le k\le p+1$
conclusions: $\rho$ arises from $S_k(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}))$

nodes.name: Propagation of modularity across primes for fixed weight
nodes.statement: (i) If all 2-dimensional, mod $p$, odd, irreducible $\bar\rho$ of weight $k\le p+1$ unramified outside $p$ are modular, then for any prime $q \ge k-1$, all 2-dim, mod $q$, odd, irreducible $\bar\rho'$ of weight $k$ unramified outside $q$ are modular. (ii) If level 1 Serre's conjecture is known for an odd prime $p$, it is known for all 2-dim mod $q$ representations of weight $\le p+1$.
conclusions: (i) Modularity follows for all primes $q \ge k-1$ at the same weight
(ii) Modularity follows for all primes $q$ in the weight range $\le p+1$

nodes.name: Chebyshev's prime estimate (effective)
nodes.statement: If $\pi(x)$ is the prime counting function and $x>30$, then $A(x/\log x) \le \pi(x) \le B(x/\log x)$ with $A=0.921\ldots$ and $B/A = 6/5$. Consequently, for any $a>1.2$ and $p_n > \max(30,a^{6/(5a-6)})$, $p_{n+1} \le a p_n$.

nodes.name: Chebyshev-based existence of suitable $P_{n+1}$
nodes.statement: Given $p_n \ge 31$, there always exists a non-Fermat prime $P_{n+1}$ (either $p_{n+1}$ or $p_{n+2}$ if $p_{n+1}$ is Fermat) and an odd prime power $\ell^r = 2m+1$ dividing $P_{n+1}-1$ exactly such that $P_{n+1}/p_n \le (2m+1)/(m+1) - (m/(m+1))(1/p_n)$.

nodes.name: Key Chebyshev inequality (*)
nodes.statement: $\dfrac{P_{n+1}}{p_n} \le \dfrac{2m+1}{m+1} - \dfrac{m}{m+1}\cdot\dfrac{1}{p_n}$.

nodes.name: Local form of $\bar\rho|_{I_p}$ in ordinary case
nodes.statement: $\bar\rho|_{I_p} \cong \begin{pmatrix} \bar\chi_p^{k-1} & * \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$ with $2 \le k \le p-1$.

nodes.name: Local form of weight-2 lift $\rho|_{I_p}$
nodes.statement: $\rho|_{I_p} \cong \begin{pmatrix} \omega_p^{k-2}\chi_p & * \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$.

nodes.name: Taylor's potential modularity
nodes.statement: For an odd irreducible $\bar\rho$, there exists a totally real Galois extension $F/\mathbb{Q}$ of even degree, with prescribed local properties, such that $\bar\rho|_{G_F}$ arises from a Hilbert modular form (potentially modular).
conclusions: Existence of a totally real Galois extension $F/\mathbb{Q}$ of even degree with $\bar\rho|_{G_F}$ arising from a Hilbert modular form, with prescribed local behaviour at $p$

nodes.name: Böckle's appendix: $R \simeq O[[X_1,\ldots,X_r]]/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ with $s \le r$
nodes.statement: Local deformation conditions yielding flat, complete-intersection local rings of the prescribed relative dimension imply that the global deformation ring $R$ is a complete intersection finite flat over $O$.
assumptions: $R$ a global deformation ring with prescribed local deformation conditions
Each local deformation ring $R_\ell$ is flat, complete intersection, of relative dimension $\dim_\mathbb{F} H^0(D_\ell,\mathrm{Ad}^0(\bar\rho))+\delta_{\ell p}$
conclusions: $R$ is a complete intersection, finite flat over $O$

nodes.name: Modularity lifting (Wiles, Taylor-Wiles)
nodes.statement: If $\bar\rho$ is modular and the residual representation satisfies the relevant non-degeneracy / distinguished hypotheses, then any minimal $p$-adic lift $\rho$ is modular.
assumptions: $\bar\rho$ modular with non-degenerate / distinguished residual hypotheses
conclusions: $\rho$ is modular

nodes.name: Skinner-Wiles modularity lifting (residually reducible / ordinary)
nodes.statement: Modularity lifting in the residually reducible/ordinary cases, assuming $I_p$-distinguished residual representation.
conclusions: $\rho$ is modular

nodes.name: Kisin modularity lifting (potentially Barsotti-Tate)
nodes.statement: A modularity lifting theorem for potentially Barsotti-Tate $p$-adic lifts when the residual representation is non-degenerate.
assumptions: $\rho$ a $p$-adic lift, potentially Barsotti-Tate at $p$ over a tamely ramified extension (e.g. $\mathbb{Q}_p(\mu_p)$)
$\bar\rho$ non-degenerate: irreducible on restriction to $G_{\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{(-1)^{(p-1)/2} p})}$
conclusions: $\rho$ is modular

nodes.name: Ribet-Edixhoven weight/level optimization
nodes.statement: If $\bar\rho$ arises from some weight $k$ and level then it arises from weight $k(\bar\rho)$ and level $N(\bar\rho)$.
assumptions: $\bar\rho: G_\mathbb{Q} \to \mathrm{GL}_2(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ arises from a modular form of some weight $k$ and level $N$
conclusions: $\bar\rho$ arises from a form of weight $k(\bar\rho)$ and level $N(\bar\rho)$

nodes.name: Tate's level-1 mod 2 case of Serre's conjecture
nodes.statement: Serre's level-1 conjecture holds for $p=2$ (proved by Tate, 1973).
assumptions: $\bar\rho: G_\mathbb{Q} \to \mathrm{GL}_2(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_2)$ continuous, odd, irreducible, unramified outside 2
conclusions: No such $\bar\rho$ exists; equivalently, every such $\bar\rho$ is modular (vacuously)

nodes.name: Serre's level-1 mod 3 case
nodes.statement: Serre's level-1 conjecture holds for $p=3$ (proved by Serre, applying Tate's method).
assumptions: $\bar\rho: G_\mathbb{Q} \to \mathrm{GL}_2(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_3)$ continuous, odd, irreducible, unramified outside 3
conclusions: No such $\bar\rho$ exists; equivalently every such $\bar\rho$ is modular (vacuously)

nodes.name: KW low-weight cases of level-1 Serre
nodes.statement: Serre's level-1 conjecture holds in weights $2,4,6,8,12,14$.
assumptions: $\bar\rho: G_\mathbb{Q}\to \mathrm{GL}_2(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ continuous, odd, irreducible, level 1, with $k(\bar\rho) \in \{2,4,6,8,12,14\}$
conclusions: $\bar\rho$ arises from $S_{k(\bar\rho)}(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}))$

nodes.name: Inductive weight-reduction strategy for level-1 Serre
nodes.statement: Inductive weight-reduction procedure: starting from a level-1 mod $p$ representation $\bar\rho$, lift to weight 2, place into a compatible system, reduce mod a foil prime $\ell$, lift again with prescribed nebentype at $p$, place into another compatible system, and use modularity lifting twice to deduce modularity of $\bar\rho$.
input: A continuous, odd, irreducible 2-dim mod-$p$ representation $\bar\rho: G_\mathbb{Q}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ unramified outside $p$, with $p_n+2 \le k(\bar\rho) \le P_{n+1}+1$
Inductive hypothesis: level-1 Serre known mod $p_n$
A prime $\ell$ with $\ell^r = 2m+1$ dividing $P_{n+1}-1$ exactly, satisfying inequality (\ref{*})

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition \ref{p} (existence of weight-2 minimal lift)
nodes.statement: Reduce to non-solvable image, then verify the local versal deformation ring $R_p$ at $p$ is smooth of relative dimension $1+\dim_\mathbb{F} H^0(D_p, \mathrm{Ad}^0(\bar\rho))$ via E3, E4 of Taylor [Tay3]; combined with the global lifting machinery of Section 2.1 this yields the lift.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition \ref{q} (Galois Carayol analog)
nodes.statement: Verify two local facts: $R_p$ smooth of correct relative dimension (cited), and $R_q$ smooth of relative dimension 1 via explicit construction of a 1-parameter family of lifts using the tame relation $\sigma\tau\sigma^{-1} = \tau^q$ and a Hensel-type quadratic argument.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition \ref{c} (compatible system)
nodes.statement: Construct $(\rho_\lambda)$ via Brauer's theorem and base change (Arthur-Clozel) following Taylor [Tay2] Theorem 6.6, then refine local properties at $p,q,\ell$ using Dieulefait-Wintenberger and (in part (ii)) Raynaud's Proposition 2.3.1 plus Saito on inertial WD parameters and Breuil-Mézard / Savitt for the weight assertion.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma \ref{dihedral}
nodes.statement: Class-field-theoretic / group-theoretic analysis of dihedral images: $t$ odd forces $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-p})$ imaginary, $L/K$ unramified, and the inertia image of order 2 fixes the weight to be $(p+1)/2$; part (ii) follows because the inertia image is forced of order 2.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma \ref{breuil}
nodes.statement: Direct invocation of Breuil-Mézard Proposition 6.1.1 and Savitt Theorem 6.11: cases (i) and (iii) of loc. cit. are related by twist and Cartier dual, both ordinary.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma \ref{rubbish}
nodes.statement: Using Lemma \ref{dihedral} the only uncovered case is weight $p+1$ non-ordinary; via Berger-Li-Zhu Corollary 4.1.3 the residual representation has $\bar\rho|_{D_p}$ irreducible of Serre weight 2 -- but Theorem 4.1 of [KW] rules out level-1 weight-2 representations.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary \ref{trivial}
nodes.statement: Lift $\bar\rho'$ via Theorem 2.1 of [KW] to a crystalline weight-$k$ representation, place into a compatible system, reduce at a prime above $p$, use the hypothesis and Lemma \ref{rubbish} to conclude modularity.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{main} (general inductive argument)
nodes.statement: Inductive procedure: start with $\bar\rho$ mod $p=P_{n+1}$ of weight $k\le p+1$, reduce to ordinary at $p$, construct a weight-2 minimal lift, place in a compatible system, reduce mod a foil prime $\ell$ chosen via Chebyshev, construct a second lift with prescribed nebentype at $p$, exploit Breuil-Mézard / Savitt to control the residual weight at $p$ within the inductively-modular range, then apply modularity lifting twice.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary \ref{cond}
nodes.statement: Case $q=2$ from Theorem 4.1(ii) of [KW]; case $q\neq 2$ via 'killing ramification' (Section 5.2 of [KW]): minimal lift, compatible system, reduce mod $q$, apply Theorem \ref{main} and modularity lifting via Lemma \ref{dihedral} and Lemma \ref{breuil}.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary \ref{finite}
nodes.statement: A mod-$p$ irreducible 2-dim representation arising from $S_k(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}))$ also arises from $S_2(\Gamma_1(p^2))$, which has finitely many Hecke eigensystems.

nodes.name: Weight 8 case (mod 7)
nodes.statement: For weight 8 it suffices to prove modularity of an irreducible 2-dim mod-7 level-1 weight-8 $\bar\rho$. Lift to a weight-2 semistable $\rho$ at 7 unramified outside 7, build a compatible system, reduce mod 3 to get $\bar\rho'$ of weight 2 unramified outside 3,7; lift with nebentype $\omega_7^2$ (or $\omega_7^4$) at 7 to get $(\rho'_\lambda)$ residually at 7 of weight 4 or 6 (modular), apply lifting theorems.

nodes.name: Weights 10, 12 case (mod 11)
nodes.statement: For weights 10, 12 it suffices to handle a mod-11 representation; reduce mod 5 in the compatible system, lift with nebentype $\omega_{11}^4$ (or $\omega_{11}^6$), get residual weight 6 or 8 at 11, conclude.

nodes.name: Weights 14--20 case (mod 19)
nodes.statement: For weights 14, 16, 18, 20: use mod 19, reduce mod 3 in compatible system, lift with nebentype $\omega_{19}^8$ (or $\omega_{19}^{10}$), residual weight at 19 becomes 10 or 12, apply known cases.

nodes.name: Weights 22--30 case (mod 29)
nodes.statement: For weights 22, 24, 26, 28, 30: use mod 29, foil prime 7, lift with nebentype $\omega_{29}^{16}$ (weights 22,26,30) or $\omega_{29}^{14}$ (weights 24,28); residual weight at 29 becomes 14, 16, or 18, apply known cases.

nodes.name: Weight 32 case (mod 31)
nodes.statement: For weight 32: mod 31, foil prime 5, weight-2 compatible system $(\rho'_\lambda)$ of nebentype $\omega_{31}^{16}$ at 31; residual weight at 31 is 16 or 18, apply known cases.

nodes.name: Schoof's input that catalysed the method
nodes.statement: Schoof's results that semistable abelian varieties over $\mathbb{Q}$ with good reduction outside 17 (resp. 19) are isogenous to powers of $J_0(17)$ (resp. $J_0(19)$) led, via the KW method, to weights 18 and 20, and prompted the weight-reduction trick used here.

nodes.name: Auxiliary prime introduces no ramification
nodes.statement: The proof uses an auxiliary prime $\ell\neq p$, but no ramification is introduced at this prime, unlike in more traditional uses of auxiliary primes.

nodes.name: Quantitative bound on $N(2,p)$
nodes.statement: The number $N(2,p)$ of isomorphism classes of continuous semisimple odd $\bar\rho:G_\mathbb{Q}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ unramified outside $p$ is bounded by $C p^3$ for an absolute constant $C$. Conjecturally $N(2,p)\sim p^3/48$.

nodes.name: Inductive setup and Chebyshev choice
nodes.statement: Assume level-1 Serre is proven mod $p_n \ge 31$. By Corollary \ref{trivial}(ii) Serre is also known for any prime $q$ in weight $\le p_n+1$. Choose by Chebyshev a non-Fermat prime $P_{n+1}>p_n$ and an odd prime power $\ell^r=2m+1$ dividing $P_{n+1}-1$ exactly, with the inequality (\ref{*}) satisfied. Set $p:=P_{n+1}$; consider weight $k$ with $p_n+2\le k\le P_{n+1}+1$.

nodes.name: Reduce to ordinary at $p$ via Lemma \ref{weights}
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{weights} and using the modularity of small weights, we may assume $\bar\rho$ is ordinary at $p$.

nodes.name: Construct minimal weight-2 lift $\rho$ via Proposition \ref{p}
nodes.statement: Apply Proposition \ref{p} to construct a weight-2 minimal lift $\rho$ of $\bar\rho$ unramified outside $p$.

nodes.name: Place $\rho$ in compatible system $(\rho_\lambda)$ and reduce mod $\ell$
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{c}(i) make $\rho$ a member of a compatible system $(\rho_\lambda)$. Reduce mod a prime $\lambda$ above $\ell$ fixed by $\iota_\ell$ to get $\bar\rho_\ell$ of weight 2.

nodes.name: Easy cases: solvable or unramified at $p$
nodes.statement: If $\bar\rho_\ell$ has solvable image, modularity follows from Lemma \ref{dihedral}(i) (giving ordinary, distinguished at $\ell$) and modularity lifting theorems of Wiles, Taylor-Wiles, Skinner-Wiles. If $\bar\rho_\ell$ is unramified at $p$, the weight-2 level-1 result of [KW] forces it reducible.

nodes.name: Lift $\bar\rho_\ell$ via Proposition \ref{q} with chosen nebentype
nodes.statement: Apply Proposition \ref{q} (with role of $p$ played by $\ell$ and role of $q$ played by $p$) to obtain a lift $\rho'$ of $\bar\rho_\ell$ unramified outside $\ell,p$, Barsotti-Tate at $\ell$, with nebentype $\omega_p^j$ at $p$ where $j$ lies in the interval $((m/(2m+1))(p-1), ((m+1)/(2m+1))(p-1)]$.

nodes.name: Build second compatible system and inspect mod-$p$ reduction
nodes.statement: Use Proposition \ref{c}(ii) to build $(\rho'_\lambda)$. Consider $\rho''$ at the place above $p$ fixed by $\iota_p$: unramified outside $p$, Barsotti-Tate over $\mathbb{Q}_p(\mu_p)$.

nodes.name: Solvable/reducible residual case via Breuil-Mézard and Lemma \ref{dihedral}
nodes.statement: If $\bar{\rho}''$ is reducible at $p$, Lemma \ref{breuil} gives that $\rho''$ is ordinary up to twist and $I_p$-distinguished. If $\bar{\rho}''$ has solvable image, Lemma \ref{dihedral} yields ordinary + $I_p$-distinguished, allowing application of Skinner-Wiles and Kisin lifting theorems.

nodes.name: Non-solvable case: weight of $\bar{\rho}''$ falls in inductively-known range
nodes.statement: If $\bar{\rho}''$ has non-solvable image, Proposition \ref{c}(ii) combined with Breuil-Mézard / Savitt gives $k(\bar{\rho}'') = j+2$ or $p+1-j$; by the choice of $j$ and (\ref{*}), both intervals lie in $[2,p_n+1]$, so $\bar{\rho}''$ is modular by inductive hypothesis. Apply Kisin's lifting theorem to conclude $\rho''$ modular.

nodes.name: Transfer modularity back to $\bar\rho$
nodes.statement: Modularity of $(\rho'_\lambda)$ follows. Since $(\rho_\lambda)$ and $(\rho'_\lambda)$ are linked at the prime above $\ell$ fixed by $\iota_\ell$, modularity lifting (Wiles, Taylor-Wiles) gives modularity of $(\rho_\lambda)$, hence of $\bar\rho$ in some weight and level. Ribet/Edixhoven sharpens to weight $k(\bar\rho)$ and level 1.

nodes.name: Local deformation rings $R_p$ and $R_q$ smooth
nodes.statement: Verify $R_p$ smooth over $O$ of relative dimension $\dim_\mathbb{F} H^0(D_p,\mathrm{Ad}^0(\bar\rho))+1$ (Ramakrishna, Taylor [Tay3]); verify $R_q$ smooth of relative dimension 1 = $\dim_\mathbb{F} H^0(D_q,\mathrm{Ad}^0(\bar\rho))$.

nodes.name: Tangent-space dimension at $q$ equals 1
nodes.statement: Use Section 1 of Wiles (and Section 4.3 of de Shalit) to show $\dim_\mathbb{F}$ of mod-$\pi$ Zariski tangent space of $R_q$ is 1: dual-number lifts arising from $R_q$ coincide with the minimal lifts of Wiles.

nodes.name: Construct 1-parameter family of lifts via tame relation
nodes.statement: Choose generators $\sigma,\tau$ of the tame Galois group with $\sigma\tau\sigma^{-1}=\tau^q$. With $A=\rho_q(\sigma)$, $B=\rho_q(\tau)$ and $\chi'=\eta_q^i$ non-trivial of order dividing $q-1$, the relation reduces to $AB=BA$, giving $\alpha-\beta=\gamma(\chi'(\tau)-1)$. Combined with $\alpha\beta=\psi$, this yields the quadratic $\beta^2-\beta\gamma(\chi'(\tau)-1)-\psi=0$.

nodes.name: Hensel-type solve for $\beta$
nodes.statement: Since $\chi'(\tau)-1$ lies in the maximal ideal, for each $\gamma$ reducing to $b$ there is a unique $\beta$ congruent to $r$ mod the maximal ideal solving the quadratic, hence a unique $\alpha$. This yields a 1-parameter family in $\gamma$ of lifts $\rho_q$, proving $R_q$ smooth over $O$ of relative dimension 1.

nodes.name: Globalize via Section \ref{liftings}
nodes.statement: Combining the local smoothness of $R_p$ and $R_q$ with Böckle's principle (Proposition 1 of the appendix to [K03]) and the Hecke-algebra identification $R_F\simeq T_F$, the global deformation ring $R$ is a finite flat complete intersection over $O$, producing the desired lift.

nodes.name: Image of inertia in projective image is cyclic of order 2
nodes.statement: $H = D_{2t}$ is the projective image; since $|H|$ is prime to $p$, the image of $I_p$ is cyclic. If $t$ were even, $D_{2t}$ would have a $\mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}/2$ quotient producing a character of order 2 unramified everywhere, contradiction. So $t$ is odd, the unique character $\eta$ of order 2 cuts out a quadratic field $K$ ramified at $p$, and $\tau_p$ has order 2.

nodes.name: $K$ imaginary quadratic with non-trivial class group
nodes.statement: Oddness gives complex conjugation $c$ with non-trivial image $\gamma$, so $\eta(\gamma)\neq 1$ and $K$ is imaginary; thus $p\equiv 3\pmod 4$, and $t | h_K$.

nodes.name: Decomposition group abelian, deduce weight
nodes.statement: $\Delta_p \le H$ is abelian (quotient of Galois group of $\mathbb{Q}_{p,unr}(\sqrt{p})/\mathbb{Q}_p$); since the order-2 subgroup $\Gamma_p$ is its own centralizer, $\Delta_p = \Gamma_p$. Hence $I_p$ acts via level-1 characters, and after twisting to weight in $[2,p+1]$, $I_p$ acts with characters $1$ and $\chi_p^{k-1}$. Order 2 forces $k-1 = (p-1)/2$, i.e. $k = (p+1)/2$.

nodes.name: Reduce to BLZ-controlled remaining case
nodes.statement: Lemma \ref{dihedral} gives ordinary + distinguished in the dihedral cases. Only uncovered case: $\rho$ of weight $p+1$, non-ordinary. By Berger-Li-Zhu Corollary 4.1.3, the residual representation has $\bar\rho|_{D_p}$ irreducible of Serre weight 2.

nodes.name: Contradiction with Theorem 4.1 of [KW]
nodes.statement: But Theorem 4.1 of [KW] forbids any Serre-type $\bar\rho$ of level 1 and weight 2; contradiction.

nodes.name: Initialise inductive base
nodes.statement: Initialise: known modularity for level-1 Serre's conjecture mod every prime $\le p_n$ (with base case $p_n=31$ established in Section 6.1). Choose Chebyshev pair $(P_{n+1}, \ell)$.

nodes.name: Reduce to ordinary $\bar\rho$ at $p$
nodes.statement: Reduce input $\bar\rho$ (mod $p:=P_{n+1}$) to the ordinary case at $p$ via Lemma \ref{weights} and inductive hypothesis.

nodes.name: Construct first lift $\rho$
nodes.statement: Apply Proposition \ref{p} to build a weight-2 minimal lift $\rho$ unramified outside $p$.

nodes.name: Form first compatible system $(\rho_\lambda)$
nodes.statement: Apply Proposition \ref{c}(i) to make $\rho$ part of a weakly compatible system. Pick a foil prime $\ell$ as in initialisation and set $\bar\rho_\ell$ = reduction at the chosen prime above $\ell$.

nodes.name: Branch on $\bar\rho_\ell$ image / ramification
nodes.statement: If $\bar\rho_\ell$ has solvable image (or is unramified at $p$): apply modularity lifting theorems (Wiles, Taylor-Wiles, Skinner-Wiles) to conclude. Otherwise: continue.

nodes.name: Construct second lift $\rho'$ with chosen nebentype at $p$
nodes.statement: Apply Proposition \ref{q} to lift $\bar\rho_\ell$ to $\rho'$, unramified outside $\ell,p$, Barsotti-Tate at $\ell$, with nebentype $\omega_p^j$ at $p$ for $j$ in the prescribed Chebyshev interval.

nodes.name: Form second compatible system and reduce mod $p$
nodes.statement: Apply Proposition \ref{c}(ii) to obtain $(\rho'_\lambda)$; consider $\rho''$ at the prime above $p$ fixed by $\iota_p$ and its residual $\bar{\rho}''$.

nodes.name: Verify residual modularity of $\bar{\rho}''$ via inductive hypothesis
nodes.statement: Determine $k(\bar{\rho}'') \in \{j+2,\, p+1-j\}$ via Breuil-Mézard / Savitt and Proposition \ref{c}(ii). Inequality (\ref{*}) places this weight in $[2, p_n+1]$, so $\bar{\rho}''$ is modular by inductive hypothesis.

nodes.name: Apply modularity lifting twice; return modularity of $\bar\rho$
nodes.statement: Apply Kisin's modularity lifting theorem to $\rho''$ to deduce modularity of $(\rho'_\lambda)$. Since $(\rho_\lambda)$ and $(\rho'_\lambda)$ are linked at the prime above $\ell$, apply Wiles / Taylor-Wiles modularity lifting again to conclude modularity of $(\rho_\lambda)$ and hence of $\bar\rho$. Then Ribet / Edixhoven gives weight $k(\bar\rho)$ and level 1.
